title: 15-minute DNA extraction from beetle legs for PCR barcoding
author: Chase Mayers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmj4k4qw

steps.title: Add PrepMan reagent
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL of PrepMan Ultra Sample Preparation Reagent into a small microcentrifuge tube, label the tube, and work in a sterile environment away from PCR equipment to avoid contamination.

steps.title: Add beetle leg
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps, remove one (or multiple) beetle leg(s)—fresh, dried, or ethanol‑preserved—and place them into the tube containing the PrepMan reagent.

steps.title: Crush leg tissue
steps.instruction: With a sterile transfer needle (or similar tool), thoroughly crush the leg(s) against the inner wall of the microcentrifuge tube to homogenize.

steps.title: Heat incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 100 °C for 10 minutes (00:10:00).

steps.title: Optional centrifugation
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the tube, then transfer the supernatant to a new labeled microcentrifuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Pipette the supernatant into a new labeled microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Store or use template
steps.instruction: The supernatant is ready as PCR template; it may be used immediately or stored at –20 °C.
